data.title: Implementation of share buyback programme
data.description:
Nasdaq Copenhagen

Euronext Dublin

London Stock Exchange

Danish FSA

Date 9 October 2026

Implementation of share buyback programme

In accordance with the corporate announcement of 2 October 2026, the bank will implement a new share buyback programme of DKK 400 million for cancellation at a future general meeting.

The share buyback programme is based on the general authority which the bank’s annual general meeting of 4 March 2026 granted to the board of directors, enabling the bank to acquire its own shares.

The share buyback programme runs in the period 12 October 2026 up to and including 8 January 2027.

During the period the bank will thus buy back its own shares for a total of up to DKK 400 million under the programme, but to a maximum of 500,000 shares.

The share buyback programme will be implemented in compliance with Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 April 2014 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2016/1052 of 8 March 2016, which together constitute the Safe Harbour rules.

The bank may suspend or stop the buyback of shares at any time, in which event a corporate announcement will be issued.

The conditions for the share buyback programme are as follows:

  • The purpose of the share buyback is to adjust the bank’s capital structure.
  • Ringkjøbing Landbobank has appointed Danske Bank lead manager of the share buyback programme. Danske Bank will make all trading decisions independently, without influence from Ringkjøbing Landbobank, and will purchase shares within the published limits.
  • The maximum amount that Ringkjøbing Landbobank may pay for shares purchased under the programme is DKK 400 million, while the maximum number of shares which it may acquire under the programme is 500,000.
  • Ringkjøbing Landbobank may not purchase shares at a price exceeding the higher of (i) the price of the latest independent transaction; or (ii) the highest bid from an independent buyer on Nasdaq Copenhagen at the time of the transaction.
  • The total number of shares that Ringkjøbing Landbobank may purchase on a single trading day cannot exceed 25% of the average daily traded volume over the preceding 20 trading days on Nasdaq Copenhagen.
  • Ringkjøbing Landbobank will issue a separate weekly announcement to Nasdaq Copenhagen, in both aggregated and detailed form, stating the number and value of the shares it has purchased.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias to 'stress test' oil markets already hobbled by tight fuel supplies
data.description:
By Myra P. Saefong

Supply disruptions during the Atlantic hurricane season usually end up being a blip. This year could be very different.

Hurricane Isaias is forecast to make landfall late Friday near the Florida and Alabama border.

The oil shock created by the Iran war is about to face its first hurricane of the Atlantic storm season, which is set to hit Friday near the heart of the U.S. oil production and refining industry.

"At a time of unprecedented oil supply disruption for geopolitical reasons, Hurricane Isaias offers a reminder that weather risk hasn't disappeared," said Pavel Molchanov, investment-strategy analyst at Raymond James.

Hurricane Isaias was expected to make landfall as a Category 2 hurricane along the U.S. Gulf Coast Friday night near the Florida and Alabama border, according to AccuWeather.

Isaias already made history as the latest hurricane on record to form during the Atlantic hurricane season, which runs from June 1 through Nov. 30.

It comes at a critical time for the global oil industry. Crude-oil transits through the Strait of Hormuz have been trying to recover even as the conflict in the Middle East has stretched into an eight month, and U.S. retail prices for refined products, including gasoline and diesel have pulled back from their highs of the year.

"If this hurricane ends up causing refinery flooding, it would exacerbate an already tight market for refined products, further pushing up prices at the pump," Molchanov told MarketWatch.

The National Hurricane Center warned that dry areas near the Gulf Coast could be flooded by rising waters and that through the weekend, localized rainfall amounts of up to 15 inches are possible, particularly in parts of the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend.

As of Friday morning, Hurricane Isaias has the potential to disrupt about 6.7 million barrels of oil production, according to Tony Dupont, chief operating officer at Earth Science Associates, a provider of data and analytic tools to the companies that produce oil and gas in the Gulf of America.

The projected path is on the eastern side of the Gulf. The good news for the oil and gas industry is that most of their facilities - both onshore and offshore - are further west, said Molchanov. "The caveat here is that hurricane trajectories are subject to change."

Based on the latest projections, the coastlines of Alabama and Mississippi could be the most affected, he said. Alabama has 142,000 barrels per day of refining capacity and Mississippi has 394,000 barrels per day. Louisiana has far more, at 3 million barrels per day, he said, though the hurricane is forecast to cross over only a portion of that.

Refining flooding would be the top risk because repairing damage from that could take months, said Molchanov. With no flooding, refineries could be expected to resume operations within weeks, roughly the same recovery timetable for offshore oil production platforms, he said.

By late Thursday morning, 45.5% of the rigs in the Gulf of America had been evacuated, with nearly 63% of the region's oil production temporarily suspended, according to the Marine Minerals Administration.

"In a normal year, a precautionary shutdown of production and refining assets is basically a non event," said Rob Barnett, global head of commodity research and senior energy analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, But this year it's a "stress test given how tight markets are for diesel, jet fuel and other refined products."

Average U.S. retail prices for regular gasoline were at $4.372 a gallon Friday, down from $4.225 a month ago, while diesel cost $6.279 a gallon, after climbing to a record high at $6.528 on Sept. 22, according to AAA.

It has been an exceptionally quiet Atlantic hurricane season, broadly consistent with a strong El Niño, said Barnett, referring to a climate pattern that can lead to warmer weather. That has been a "blessing for energy markets, given the Strait of Hormuz disruptions and other dislocations in the global market."

-Myra P. Saefong

data.title: Could Smartphone Ownership Among Children Increase Risk Of Eating Disorder Symptoms?
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - A new study published in JAMA Network Open involving nearly 9,000 teenagers in the U.S. found that children who owned a smartphone at age 12 were more likely to report symptoms of eating disorders later.

The researchers analyzed data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study, a large US research project that tracks brain development and health in children and teenagers. Of the total participants, about 70 percent owned a smartphone at age 12, while the remaining did not.

The researchers examined four types of eating disorder symptoms when the participants were 12 and 14 years old. These included binge eating, behaviors intended to prevent weight gain, fear of gaining weight and judging one's self-worth based on body weight.

Two years later, the researchers found a clear difference between the two groups. At age 14, 24.2 percent of teenagers who owned a smartphone at age 12 reported at least one of the symptoms studied. In comparison, only 15.5 percent of those who did not own a smartphone at age 12 reported such symptoms.

The researchers also considered other factors that could influence the results, which included gender, family income, parents' education levels, body weight, puberty, symptoms of depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), parental monitoring and ownership of other digital devices. They also accounted for eating disorder symptoms that the children had already experienced at age 12.

Even after considering these factors, owning a smartphone at age 12 was associated with a 49 percent higher risk of reporting at least one eating disorder symptom at age 14.

When the researchers examined individual symptoms, they found that smartphone ownership at age 12 was associated with a 67 percent higher risk of binge eating two years later. It was also linked to a 50 percent higher risk of engaging in behaviors intended to prevent weight gain.

Additionally, teenagers who owned smartphones at age 12 were approximately twice as likely to base their self-worth on their body weight.

'Owning a personal smartphone during early adolescence may be particularly consequential, given its potential to increase unsupervised and individualized exposure to digital environments during a sensitive developmental period,' the study authors explained.

'These influences may also accumulate over time and be shaped by developmental timing.'

data.title: Global Bond Yields Edge Higher on Slowing Bond Selloff — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha and Paulo Trevisani

U.S. and European yields rose Friday, but stayed below recent highs as the global bonds selloff eased.

Well-received 10-year and 30-year bond auctions in the U.S. indicated prices, which move in the opposite direction of yields, may have become cheap enough to attract buyers.

"It's been a good week for U.S. bond auctions," ING's Padhraic Garvey, regional head of research for the Americas, and Benjamin Schroeder, senior rates strategist, said in a note. "Solid 10-year and 30-year auctions over consecutive days show there is a level where buyers step in."

Markets will be watching inflation data next week. The U.S. September consumer price index on Wednesday will be one of the last relevant data points before the Federal Reserve's next meeting, when the central bank is expected to keep rates on hold.

The 10-year Treasury yield traded at 5.253%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.607%, according to Tradeweb. Both were on pace for a small weekly decline. They reached 24-year highs of 5.365% and 5.733%, respectively, earlier this week.

In the eurozone, the German 10-year Bund yield ticked higher to 3.477% from 3.452%. French bonds rose to 4.854% from 4.795%.

Concerns about France remain due to doubts about the government's ability to reduce the budget deficit target to 5% of gross domestic product in 2027 due to a fragmented parliament. The government's plans to cut expenditure are among a number of factors which have prompted nationwide demonstrations in France.

Investors are also wary due to the country's upcoming plans for a significant amount of bond issuance.

France will issue bonds again on Thursday next week. Hefty supply will likely maintain selling pressure on OATs and keep yields high, Citi rates strategist Jamie Searle and Puja Sawant said in a note.

Issuance looks set to be particularly hefty early next year, which might concern investors, they said. The French Treasury Agency said in late September that it had penciled in 340 billion euros ($381.23 billion) in medium- and long-term government bond issuance, net of buybacks, for 2027. This target volume compares with this year's issuance target of 310 billion euros.

The outlook for global government bonds overall looks brighter, however, after yields on many major developed-market bonds recently surged to multiyear highs, Benoit Anne, head of market insights at MFS Investment Management, said in a note.

Markets might have gone too far in pricing in interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, leaving scope for some retracement and a potential relief rally in government bonds, he said. Money markets fully price in three rate increases in the next 12 months, LSEG data showed.

"This may help cap the upside risks to rates from the standpoint of monetary policy," he said. The recent upward momentum in long-dated U.S. yields appears to have slowed somewhat, although fiscal challenges persist, he said.

data.title: Wireless Carriers' Day of Woe After SpaceX Spectrum Deal — WSJ
data.description:
By Patience Haggin

Shares in AT&T, Verizon Communications and T-Mobile US fell sharply Friday in the wake of SpaceX's $8 billion spectrum deal, the Elon Musk-led company's biggest move yet into the wireless market.

By early afternoon AT&T and Verizon were on track for their biggest one-day declines in more than 24 years. For T-Mobile, it would be the worst percentage drop in more than 13 years.

SpaceX said Thursday it had agreed to buy cellular spectrum licenses from investment firm Grain Management-specifically, spectrum that can cover places satellite links can't reach, like inside buildings. SpaceX has said it wants to move its Starlink satellite service beyond broadband, and this acquisition could make it a more serious threat to the leading consumer wireless carriers.

Starlink already provides internet connectivity via thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, as well as basic wireless connections in remote areas through a T-Mobile partnership.

data.title: Port of Los Angeles sets September volume record, executive director says
data.description:
By Lisa Baertlein

The Port of Los Angeles, the busiest in the US for containers, set a volume record in September as holiday goods hit docks, ships were routed away from the drought-stricken Panama Canal and importers picked the shortest route from China to reduce use of pricey fuel, Executive Director Gene Seroka said on Friday.

Workers at the facility handled 1.04 million 20-foot equivalent units (TEUs) during the month. Loaded containers accounted for almost 547,000 TEUs, also a new record, Seroka said.

Experts view US import data as an indicator of national economic health, consumer demand and reactions to trade policies.

"Tariffs are lower than the levels we saw earlier this year and last, giving importers more certainty on costs and allowing them to replenish inventories at a quicker rate," Seroka said of US import levies that have disrupted trade.

Total US container imports hit 2.55 million TEUs in September, a record for the month, according to supply-chain technology provider Descartes Systems .

US consumers have continued to spend, even as prices for necessities like food and energy have marched higher. Retailers account for roughly 50% of container volume, and the National Retail Federation forecast total 2026 retail sales of $5.6 trillion, up 4.4% from last year.

Shipments of equipment related to artificial intelligence projects, including components used to cool data centers, also are booming.

The surge in demand, however, has not benefited all container ports equally.

Some ships from Asia have shifted to the West Coast from the East Coast due to restrictions on the Panama Canal shortcut, said Seroka, who added that the West Coast route is the fastest for trade with that export powerhouse.

The Los Angeles port covers 7,500 acres (about 3,000 hectares) of combined land and water and lately has handled more containers than it did during the COVID-19 shipping surge, without the bottlenecks that led to more than 100 ships waiting to enter.

The port will process about 900,000 TEUs in October, said Seroka, who added that most holiday merchandise should be in the country by November.

While the near-term outlook for trade at the port remains strong, risks remain, he said.

"What could cause it to change? Another social media post or announcement on trade from Washington that could create some sort of uncertainty once again."

data.title: Marvell Stocks Fall as $20 Billion Goal Tests Execution
data.description:
Marvell Technology , the data-center networking and custom-silicon designer, traded at $271.19 at 10.50am EST, down approximately 1.3% on Friday, October 9, as investors weighed ambitious growth plans against an already demanding valuation. According to Investor's Business Daily, the company's investor-day forecasts prompted analysts to raise their price targets. The valuation snapshot puts shares 119.94% above the $123.30 GF Value, suggesting a substantial growth premium is already baked in.

Management's investor-day presentation laid out a $20 billion revenue goal for fiscal 2028, with $18 billion coming from data centers. That compares with fiscal 2026 revenue of $8.2 billion overall and $6.1 billion from data centers. The total-sales target requires roughly 56% annual compounded growth over two years. Further out, management sees fiscal 2031 revenue reaching $70 billion to $90 billion. Those are company targets, and hitting them demands sustained execution as the business scales.

The analyst targets cited by Investor's Business Daily span $270 at Goldman Sachs, $350 at TD Cowen and $425 at Oppenheimer. At $271.19, shares already sit near Goldman's objective. The higher targets leave considerably more upside, but depend on stronger expectations for custom accelerators, optical connectivity and networking. That spread frames the investment debate: how much of the AI spending boom can Marvell turn into revenue and earnings? With a hefty valuation premium already in place, delivery matters more than another big forecast.

data.title: ASML Stocks Rise as Hyper-NA Shrinks AI-Chip Limits
data.description:
ASML Holding , the EUV lithography equipment leader, advanced its Hyper-NA research with optics partner Zeiss, while U.S. shares traded up approximately 1% at $1,788.51 around 12:16 p.m. ET Friday. The ambition is clear: help chipmakers squeeze smaller circuitry into future AI processors. The revenue payoff is much further out. Engineers estimate the technology could take roughly a decade to reach commercial readiness.

According to Reuters, a peer-reviewed paper puts potential feature sizes at five nanometers, more than one-third smaller than those possible with current High-NA technology. Researchers also see a path to retaining the existing EUV light source, and Zeiss can already produce mirrors with the required precision. Those are useful building blocks. They do not settle the harder questions of production speed, economics or customer demand. ASML has started development without committing to commercial production.

The valuation leaves little room for patience: the shares sit 40.5% above the roughly $1,270 GF Value estimate, signaling that investors already price in considerable growth. Reusing existing technology could reduce some development hurdles, but Hyper-NA remains a distant opportunity. The nearer checkpoint is October 14. Investors need evidence that current equipment demand and High-NA adoption can support earnings while the next generation stays in development.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias Is Moving These Power Stocks as It Barrels Toward Gulf Coast — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

The first major hurricane set to hit the mainland U.S. in two years hasn't even hit yet, but it's already moving the stocks of businesses that could be affected by it. That could create a short-term stock trading opportunity.

Isaias it set to bring flash flooding and winds up to 120 mph along the Gulf Coast when it makes landfall late Friday or early Saturday. As residents in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, and Mississippi prepare for rainfall of up to 15 inches and storm surges of up to seven feet, according to estimates from the National Hurricane Center, the risk of downed power lines and related outages is already affecting stocks in the sector.

Shares of Quanta Services, which builds and maintains power lines, were up 1.5% Friday, while MasTec, which builds and designs power equipment for utilities, fell 1.7%.

Quanta's move could be part of a historical pattern pointed out by Citi analysts on Friday. They found that engineering and construction stocks like Quanta and MasTec "outperform in the short-term when there are significant disruptive storms."

More specifically, they found the sector outperforms the S&P 500 by 1% in the five days before a big storm makes landfall, followed by a 2% outperformance during the 10-day period after large storms as the companies benefit from restoration work.

Quanta has tended to see the largest bump of around 4% in the days after a storm, but that impact could be muted this time around since storm work as a percentage of total sales is likely smaller as the company has expanded beyond its core electrical transmission and distribution business in recent years.

data.title: SEC Charges California Investment Advisor in Alleged Cherry-Picking Scheme — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

The Securities and Exchange Commission has charged a California registered investment advisor firm and its owner with an alleged cherry-picking scheme that regulators say allocated losing trades to clients while the advisor pocketed the proceeds from profitable transactions.

The charges against Darren Caris and Caris Investment Partners, based in the San Diego suburb of Encinitas, allege that Caris traded clients' funds through a block-trading account, enabling him to allocate trades to the various accounts over which he had discretion.

"Caris submitted these allocations to a brokerage firm well after he placed the trades and observed share-price movement, giving him the opportunity to 'cherry-pick' — that is, disproportionately allocate winning trades to his personal account and disproportionately allocate losing trades to 16 client accounts," the SEC says in its complaint.

The SEC alleges that from December 2023 through April 2024, Caris allocated more than $158,000 in profitable trades to his personal account, while "client accounts suffered approximately $143,754 in first-day losses because of Caris' fraud." A statistical analysis found a less than one-in-a-million chance that those trading allocations could have resulted from random chance, "as opposed to knowing and intentional conduct," according to the SEC.

Caris' lawyer, Robert Brownlie, says his client denies the allegations and "did not engage in 'cherry picking.'" Brownlie says that commission staffers explained during the investigation that their allegations were based on a statistical analysis of just three client accounts over a period of four months.

"That analysis did not show that Mr. Caris allocated trades after the outcomes were known but only that it was statistically improbable that the allocation of trades was random," Brownlie says. "Indeed, the allocation was not random."

Brownlie says that Caris distinguished his own trades from those of his clients and ensured that all trades were properly allocated. He says that the three clients involved in the statistical analysis that the SEC presented during the investigation made more than $375,000 during the relevant period. "Mr. Caris intends to defend and vindicate himself against the Commission's allegations," he says.

The case is the latest reminder that cherry-picking remains a top concern for regulators and law-enforcement authorities. Earlier this week, the SEC asked a court to approve a final judgment against Kenneth Leech, a prominent bond fund manager and the former co-chief investment officer at Western Asset Management Company, a unit of Franklin Templeton, for his role in an alleged cherry-picking scheme that saw hundreds of millions of dollars allocated to preferred or disfavored client accounts based on the performance of the trades. A representative of Franklin Templeton didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the Western Asset settlement.

The proposed settlement would require Leech to pay a $3 million penalty and accept a bar from the industry. In June, the SEC announced a settlement with Western Asset, which agreed to pay $100 million to address the cherry-picking allegations without admitting or denying wrongdoing.

In a criminal matter, Leech has pleaded guilty to obstruction of justice for providing false and misleading testimony in the SEC's investigation. He is awaiting sentencing. Lawyers for Leech declined to comment on the case.

Another recent cherry-picking case involved William Carlton, a former Cetera advisor whom the SEC accused of claiming $5.3 million in profitable trades for himself while saddling his clients with losing trades. In September, Carlton pleaded guilty to securities fraud in a criminal case. His sentencing is scheduled for January 27. Carlton's lawyer didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

In the case of Caris and his RIA, the scale of the alleged fraud is far smaller than Leech or Carlton, but the case aligns with the direction the SEC says it is taking under Chairman Paul Atkins, who has said the commission should focus more on rooting out investor fraud than pursuing settlements with financial services firms for technical rule violations that amount to no direct investor harm.

This isn't Caris' first run-in with securities regulators.

Last October, Caris settled charges with California authorities who accused him of defrauding his own children, saying that he improperly siphoned money out of their accounts for his personal use. California had initially sought to bar Caris from the industry, but the parties later reached a settlement fining the advisor $10,000 and ordering him to pay $167,000 in disgorgement — $119,000 to one of his children and $48,000 to the other. Caris reached that settlement without admitting or denying wrongdoing.

data.title: Mumbai airlines want T1 safety reports and T2 expansion clarity on 13 October agenda
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 9 -- Airlines operating out of Mumbai want the airport operator to share independent structural-safety reports on Terminal 1 (T1), clarify the status of planned capacity expansion at Terminal 2 (T2), and explain whether alternatives were considered before proposing to shift several international flights to a second airport about 50 km from the city airport, ahead of a stakeholder meeting scheduled for 13 October.

In an email sent on Friday evening to the chief airport officer's office at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA), the Airline Operators Committee-Mumbai (AOC-Mumbai), which represents all airlines operating out of Mumbai airport, proposed six agenda items for discussions with Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) on T1's redevelopment. Mint has reviewed a copy of the email.

The call to detail agenda items ahead of the 13 October meeting comes after the ministry of civil aviation (MoCA) paused the airport operator's plan to temporarily relocate the international departures and asked Adani Airport to work with airlines and agree on a transition plan.

Both AOC-Mumbai and Adani Airport were yet to respond to emails from Mint at the time of publishing.

Adani-run Mumbai city airport had planned to move a third of international flights from T2 to the new Navi Mumbai International Airport, citing T1 redevelopment. Mumbai airport operator MIAL, a joint venture between Adani Airports Holdings Ltd and the Airports Authority of India, suggested that 46 airlines move 265 of 770 weekly international flights to Navi Mumbai Airport starting 25 October. It said the released international capacity was intended to accommodate domestic operations displaced from T1 during redevelopment. For context, all international departures out of Mumbai are from T2.

Both Mumbai and Navi Mumbai airports are run by Adani Airport, India's second-largest private airport operator by revenue, after GMR Airports.

AOC-Mumbai wants MIAL to share the independent consultant reports cited in discussions about T1's structural condition. "There have been references to the structural safety of T1 by MIAL at various forums. The AOC would like to review any independent consultant reports that have established such concerns," the email said.

The committee has also asked MIAL to present a detailed redevelopment plan covering the scope of work, phased execution, technical assessments, firm timelines and the anticipated impact on airport capacity.

Airlines have reiterated their support for the redevelopment but want access to the technical evidence underpinning the plan. They have sought an update on the previously envisaged additional capacity of approximately 5 million passengers per annum (mppa) at T2, including the proposed scope and implementation timeline. They have also requested monthly data on actual capacity utilization at both terminals in 2026, alongside their available or declared capacity.

"The current status of the previously envisaged additional approximately 5 mppa T2 capacity may also kindly be clarified, including the proposed scope and implementation timeline," AOC-Mumbai said in its email. The status of the proposed T2 expansion could be relevant to discussions on accommodating domestic passengers displaced by the redevelopment of T1.

The airlines have also asked MIAL to explain what alternatives it considered, including a temporary passenger-processing facility, as part of its demand-capacity assessment for T1 and T2. They have also proposed a formal review of compliance with the civil aviation ministry's slot-allocation guidelines in the event of a capacity reduction.

The other items cover the detailed T1 redevelopment plan disclosure, capacity assessment at both terminals, the proposed methodology for reduction in international departures, and other matters related to the redevelopment.

MIAL plans to start rebuilding Terminal 1B in January 2027. Under the plan, domestic flights from Terminal 1 would move to Terminal 2, and some of Mumbai's international flights would move to Navi Mumbai.

Airlines support the rebuilding but disagree with the cut in international flights. AOC-Mumbai has questioned the technical and practical reasons for the 33% reduction. It has asked for detailed studies on capacity, demand, and planned improvements at Terminal 2. Airlines say their support for rebuilding Terminal 1 should not be seen as an agreement to remove or move international flight times already planned for the winter schedule.

Adani Airport says the move is temporary and necessary for the rebuilding, and that it will bring back old flight times with extra capacity once the new terminal opens. It says about 91% of passenger traffic will stay the same, with around 5 million passengers, or 9% of yearly traffic, temporarily moved.

The rebuilt Terminal 1 is expected to handle 20 million passengers a year, a third more than it does now. Mumbai airport handled about 38 million domestic and more than 16 million international passengers in financial year 2026.

OTTAWA--Canada's government raised 2 billion Canadian dollars (US$1.4 billion) with the sale of its seventh green bond.

The Department of Finance priced the 10-year Canadian dollar-denominated bond as part of the government's effort to unlock private capital to help speed up projects such as nature conservation and environment-focused infrastructure.

data.title: Why Today's Fruits And Vegetables May Not Be As Nutritious As Those 60 Years Ago?
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - A study by researchers at Deep Science Ventures found that people may need to eat twice as many fruits and vegetables today to get the same amount of minerals, such as potassium, magnesium and copper, as they did 60 years ago.

Using historical food data and crop records, including wheat samples collected over 160 years, the researchers identified a decline in the mineral and protein content of many important foods, which means people may need to consume more food to obtain the same amount of nutrients as previous generations.

The researchers found that several common foods, including bread, cereals, carrots, apples and peas, had lost between 20% and 50% of some important nutrients.

Nutrient deficiencies can also have serious economic and health consequences. According to the study, they cost countries up to 3% of their gross domestic product each year through reduced productivity and higher healthcare expenses. A lack of essential nutrients may also increase the risk of chronic diseases and affect maternal health and children's development.

The researchers warned that the problem could worsen in the coming decades. Rising levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, declining soil quality and farming practices that focus mainly on increasing crop yields could further reduce the nutritional value of food.

To address the problem, the researchers suggested that governments should focus not only on producing enough food but also on ensuring that food provides sufficient nutrients. They recommended setting up nationwide systems to monitor nutrient levels in crops and encouraging farming practices that improve soil health.
